data.body:
Both children closed; story complete.

Delivered:
- 7ab3-9df0-7a90-4ffd — blocking-link comparability is now structural (nearest common ancestor with a virtual-root sentinel), replacing the type-tier rule. The four tier helpers are gone, _get_ancestors is uncapped and cycle-guarded, and is_redundant is recomputed from the RESOLVED pair so an escalation landing on an ancestor is refused. Merged 693a6bf41.
- 9ad7-d5a2-a664-4827 — the audit/repair check, shipped as the first check of `rebar doctor`. Merged across 1028, 1039, 1040, 1045, 1047, 1052.

Success criteria:
- Comparability decides from the parent hierarchy alone; _TYPE_TIER is deleted. MET.
- No blocking edge can exist between a ticket and its own ancestor/descendant, by any path into the resolver. MET — enforced in the resolver itself, so add_dependency, the dry-run preview and the standalone resolve path all inherit it.
- Legacy edges detectable store-wide and repairable in one pass. MET — 18 found on this tracker, 12 repaired, 8 residual and provably inert (every endpoint closed, so none can reach ready/next-batch).
- The escalation contract is unchanged for callers. MET — cross-subtree links still auto-escalate and still emit the redirect record.

Scope changes made at operator direction, both recorded on the doctor epics:
1. A standalone link-audit verb was rejected for core; the command became `rebar doctor`, framed as a named check list so later checks slot in beside `dependency-graph` rather than each needing a verb.
2. Re-parenting invalidating the dependency graph is in scope for the doctor epic — either auto-remediate or deny with a clear error. Evidence: after remediating to zero scheduling-affecting findings, two NEW mis-escalated edges with OPEN endpoints appeared within hours. Comparability is structural, so changing a parent silently invalidates previously-correct links without touching them; the store drifts on its own.

Both doctor epics (dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6, 18ae-4f54-a85b-4ddb) are linked relates_to and carry the current command status plus what it deliberately does NOT do yet — no check registry, no crash isolation, no per-check timeouts, no config/environment/sync categories.

Honest note on execution: this took seven changes, five of which were pure test coverage for behaviour I had shipped but never pinned. The acceptance criteria named those checks; the implementation did not follow through, and only the completion-verifier close gate caught it — plan review and code review both passed the gaps.
